steps.headline: Build the money page like this: warnings first, then four totals, a net-worth chart, accounts by kind, and bills by due date.
steps.changed: A new page built from your answers, with made-up numbers. One warning row per account, so a card with three problems is one row. Each warning has its own button: Reconnect for a broken bank link, Update for a number you enter.
steps.notice: The top of the page answers "does anything need me today?"; scroll for card limits (bars turn amber past 30%, red past 80%), loans and every bill with days left.
steps.risk: The numbers here are fake. Which banks actually connect is unknown until you sign up for Plaid.

steps.path: Pages, then Money (in the practice app)
steps.headline: Try it: open Pages, then Money, and press Update on the Earnest student loan to change its balance.
steps.notice: This is the practice app: nothing you change is saved and the banks are pretend. Clicking around tells us whether the layout and buttons feel right.

steps.path: The page buttons along the top of the window, and the Pages list
steps.headline: Should the money page get its own icon instead of sharing the bar-chart one?
steps.today: Pages pick from eight icons. The money page uses the bar chart, the same one as the YouCoded analytics page.
steps.problem: The tester found the two buttons along the top almost identical and opened the wrong one.
steps.proposal: Yes adds a money icon (a dollar sign) that any page can use. No keeps the bar chart.
